title: Cloud console: verify tenant identity instead of trusting unverified JWT claims
description:
Problem: anyone on the internet can read any cloud tenant's board and realtime stream. decode_jwt_claims (rust/src/bin/console_lambda.rs:234-241) base64-decodes the middle JWT segment with no signature, issuer, audience or expiry check, and enforce_tenant_claims (:244-272) compares those claims to the URL path. The CDK stack mounts the console proxy with AuthorizationType.NONE on root and {proxy+} (infra/cloud/kanbus_cloud/cloud_stack.py:701-717); the Cognito authorizer is attached only to token-admin routes. The unit tests at console_lambda.rs:846-915 build unsigned tokens and assert they pass. The IoT custom authorizer has the same gap: _tenant_from_cognito_access_token (infra/cloud/lambda/mqtt_authorizer.py:113-146, 222-250) decodes without verifying and token signing is disabled (cloud_stack.py:980, coordination_stack.py:226). The identity-pool role grants IoT subscribe and receive on topicfilter/projects/*/*/events for every tenant plus execute-api:Invoke on * (cloud_stack.py:732-777); infra/cloud/tests/test_auth_isolation.py:40-50 asserts the wildcard. The webhook handler uses one shared secret for all tenants and takes repo_url from the payload while tenant comes from the path (infra/cloud/lambda/webhook_handler.py:72-97), so one tenant can overwrite another's EFS checkout. The console Lambda is in an isolated subnet with no NAT or endpoints, so it cannot fetch JWKS itself; the fix has to be at the gateway.

Work:
1. Attach the Cognito authorizer to the console root and {proxy+} methods, keeping /assets, /auth/* and /api/auth/bootstrap public; in the Lambda, read tenant claims from requestContext.authorizer.claims and delete the decode_jwt_claims trust path. Update the unit tests so an unsigned token is rejected.
2. In mqtt_authorizer.py verify signature, iss, aud and exp against the user-pool JWKS (PyJWT with cached keys) or always call cognito-idp GetUser and ignore decoded claims; enable authorizer token signing.
3. Scope the identity-pool role ARNs to the principal's account and project via principal tags, or remove the identity-pool path and rely on the fixed custom authorizer; fix the test that asserts the wildcard.
4. Per-tenant webhook secrets (one Secrets Manager entry per account/project) or a tenant-to-repository allowlist checked against repository.full_name.
5. Run the infra/cloud/tests suite in CI (it is currently never executed).
Also stop sending the id token as an access_token query parameter for SSE (apps/console/src/api/client.ts:113-121) and storing it in localStorage (auth/cloudAuth.ts:70-72), or document why it is acceptable until SSE is replaced by MQTT.

Acceptance: a forged token is rejected with 401 at the gateway and in the Lambda unit tests; a Cognito user from account A cannot read or subscribe to account B; infra/cloud tests pass in CI.
